transcript.text: washing machine making a horrible noise
From what you have described, the most likely cause is load size / distribution (imbalance). Next: Try an ordinary evenly-distributed load to rule out load imbalance. Let me know what you find.
It's not a load thing, it does it every spin now, even with normal loads. Got worse over a couple of months. Is it worth fixing?

It depends on the specific cause and cost of repair versus replacing the machine. If the issue is a worn bearing or motor, repairs can be expensive, often making replacement more economical for older units. From what you have described, the most likely cause is drum bearings / bearing seal. Next: With the power off, rotate the drum by hand for roughness/rumble and check for up/down play (bearing) or off-centre wobble (spider). Let me know what you find.
Spun it by hand with the power off - it rumbles/grinds as it turns. And when I lift the edge of the drum up and down there's a noticeable clunky bit of play.

From what you have described, the most likely cause is drum bearings. Let's see whether the machine itself can spin: take the washing out and run a spin-only programme with the drum empty. Does it spin up properly when it's empty?
Yes it spins empty, but it's just as loud, the noise is the drum. It still washes, drains and finishes fine though.

[Heading: Likely cause: drum bearing]
The checks point to the drum bearing. To find the right part, could you give me the make and model number? It is usually on a sticker inside the door rim or on the back of the door.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
It's a Zanussi, model ZWF81443W, off the door label. Is it worth fixing though? It's about 9 years old.

[Heading: Likely cause: drum bearing]
Given the appliance is nine years old and shows significant bearing play, repair costs often approach or exceed the value of a new machine. It may be more economical to replace it rather than invest in major internal repairs. The checks point to the drum bearing. I could not find a confirmed match for model ZWF81443W in our parts catalogue, so check with the manufacturer or a parts supplier using the full model number, or ask an appliance engineer to fit it.
